title: Memory Allocation Under Hardware Compression
problem: Hardware memory compression decouples OS-managed physical memory from actual DRAM, but lacks a specialized allocation interface for the newly-formed actual memory layer. This imprecision causes incorrect allocation decisions that harm performance by either starving jobs of actual memory or over-allocating to some jobs at the expense of others in congested memory systems.
motivation: As physical memory density scaling slows, hardware memory compression enables logical scaling by having the memory controller encode and store data more densely in DRAM.
method: The authors design a specialized memory allocation interface for the actual memory layer introduced by hardware compression. They architect an MMU-like component within the memory controller that manages precise allocation based on per-page compressibility. The system dynamically adjusts DRAM allocation per physical page depending on content compressibility. A full-system FPGA prototype validates the approach on multi-job colocation scenarios.
key_novelty: First specialized memory allocation interface and MMU-like memory controller component designed specifically to manage the actual memory layer decoupled from physical memory in hardware-compressed systems.
contributions: Identifies the absence of a specialized allocation interface for hardware-compressed memory as a critical system design gap
Designs a novel memory allocation mechanism tailored to the actual memory layer with per-page dynamic DRAM adjustment
Architects an MMU-like component in the memory controller to enforce precise allocation guarantees
Achieves 1-2% performance variation under job colocation versus 19-89% for prior approaches via full-system FPGA prototype

metrics.other: 1-2% performance variation under colocation (vs 19-89% for prior art)

limitations: Limitations are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Precise memory allocation for hardware-compressed systems
